solution_sketch: Use log_b(x) + log_b(y) = log_b(xy). Then log_6(2) + log_6(3) = log_6(6) = 1. The trap is trying to evaluate each logarithm on its own — neither term is nice, but 2·3 lands exactly on the base.
difficulty_rationale: Naive route: try to evaluate log_6(2) ≈ 0.387 and log_6(3) ≈ 0.613 — clumsy without a calculator and the near-1 sum only hints at the trick. The insight is the sum-to-product identity plus the observation that 2·3 = 6 (the base itself), collapsing the whole expression to log_6(6) = 1. One identity, one mental multiplication, one recognition — findable cold in under 20 seconds by anyone who has met logarithms, but not a two-second read.
